Write a lively dialogue that sounds like two friends who know the topic, not a press release:
- open with a hook, end with a short sign-off;
- short spoken lines, interruptions, reactions, a bit of humour; the two personalities must clash a little;
- every fact must come from the numbered sources, and the line must list those source numbers; never add facts, scores or results the sources do not state;

Topic: League of Legends Worlds 2026: the knockout stage starts
Tone: fun, for fans who missed the Swiss stage
Length: about 300 words.

Sources:

[1] 2026 League of Legends World Championship: venues and format (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_League_of_Legends_World_Championship)
Hosted in the United States, 15 October to 14 November 2026. Play-in at Riot Games Arena, Los Angeles (15-18 October). Swiss stage, quarterfinals and semifinals at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas. Final on 14 November at Barclays Center, Brooklyn, New York City. 19 teams. Swiss stage: 16 teams, three wins advance, three losses eliminated. Knockout stage: 8 teams, single elimination, all best-of-five. Base prize pool: 5,000,000 US dollars, 1,000,000 for the winner.

[2] 2026 League of Legends World Championship: Swiss stage results (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_League_of_Legends_World_Championship)
Qualified for the knockout stage: Gen.G (Korea, 3-0), Dplus KIA (Korea, 3-0), T1 (Korea, 3-1), Invictus Gaming (China, 3-1), Top Esports (China, 3-1), Karmine Corp (Europe, 3-2), LYON (North America, 3-2), Bilibili Gaming (China, 3-2). Eliminated include G2 Esports (Europe, 1-3), Movistar KOI (Europe, 2-3) and Hanwha Life Esports (Korea, 2-3). T1 are the three-time defending world champions. LYON reached the Worlds playoffs for the first time.

[3] 2026 League of Legends World Championship: Karmine Corp (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_League_of_Legends_World_Championship)
Karmine Corp (French organisation, LEC) played its first World Championship. It came through the play-in (beat Cloud9 KIA 3-2, then MVK Esports 3-0 twice). In the Swiss stage it beat Anyone's Legend, lost to LYON, lost to Bilibili Gaming, then beat CTBC Flying Oyster 2-0 and Movistar KOI 2-0 to qualify at 3-2. First knockout stage appearance for a French-based organisation since Against All Authority in 2011.

[4] 2026 League of Legends World Championship: quarterfinal schedule (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_League_of_Legends_World_Championship)
Quarterfinals, best-of-five: 3 November Top Esports vs Invictus Gaming; 4 November Gen.G vs LYON; 5 November Dplus KIA vs Bilibili Gaming; 6 November Karmine Corp vs T1. Semifinals on 7 and 8 November. No quarterfinal result is known at the time of writing.

body.input: Jane, the knockout stage is here! Eight teams left, all best-of-fives, and the first quarterfinal is already done—Top Esports versus Invictus Gaming on the third of November!
Yes, Paul, and we’re still waiting for the rest. Gen.G plays LYON on the fourth, Dplus KIA faces Bilibili Gaming on the fifth, and then—
And then the big one: Karmine Corp versus T1 on the sixth! T1 are the three-time defending champions, but Karmine Corp just made history as the first French org in the knockout stage since 2011!

Oh, please. T1’s still the favourite. But fine, let’s celebrate Karmine Corp—first Worlds for them, first knockout for a French team in over a decade. They scraped through play-ins and Swiss, but here they are.
Scraped? They beat Cloud9 KIA and MVK Esports in play-ins, then took down Movistar KOI and CTBC Flying Oyster in Swiss. That’s not luck, Jane!
Fair. But let’s not forget the prize pool: five million dollars, with a million going to the winner. That’s serious motivation.
And the final’s at Barclays Center on the fourteenth of November! Can you imagine the atmosphere?
I can imagine the hype. But for now, let’s see who survives the next few days.
Agreed. This is going to be epic. See you next time!
